caption: I owe R54 000 across five accounts and I know the order I should pay in. Do you pay the biggest one first or the smallest?

slides.title:
How I'm clearing
R54 000 of debt
on R23 100 p/m
Living in Phuthaditjhaba
slides.body:
Male, 38
Single, two daughters (13 and 9)
Job: Truck driver, building supplies depot
Net salary: R23 100 p/m
Debt: R54 000 across five accounts

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: His girls come every second weekend, so two bedrooms isn't a luxury.

slides.title: Debt payments
slides.includes: Personal loan, two store accounts, a credit card, a clothing account
slides.body: The loan has the highest interest, the clothing account has the smallest balance. I'm still deciding which one gets the extra.

slides.title: Child maintenance
slides.body: It's the first thing that leaves the account and I'm fine with that.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Monthly shop, plus weekend food when the girls are here
slides.body: The girls' weekends add R600. I wouldn't change it.

slides.title: Fuel & transport
slides.includes: Travel to the depot, the odd trip to see my mother
slides.body: The company truck is for work. My own bakkie is for everything else, and it drinks.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: black tax, prepaid electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, airtime, takeaways
slides.body: Six lines that came to R3 050. The takeaways are R950 of that and I'm not proud of it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R23 100. It's enough to pay off one small store account in about four months. I counted.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I put all five debts into Beyond Horizon's debt tracker and compared avalanche with snowball.

The total interest was different between the two. Seeing both side by side made the choice easier.

No bank login needed.
